title: AstroRegolith: an open database and growth-anchored reanalysis of plant growth in lunar, Martian and asteroid regolith
description:
An open, server-free database for plant growth in regolith, with the analysis and manuscript that accompany it.

Catalogue. Every regolith-relevant dataset in NASA's Open Science Data Repository (nine biological studies) and Physical Sciences Informatics system (six curated investigations), with measured file and image counts and a stated reason for inclusion. Only two of the nine deposit plant imagery, and PSI holds no plant-in-regolith data at all — both facts are reported rather than glossed.

Substrates. Soil-probe response of eight candidate growth substrates during watering, the LHS-1 lunar highlands simulant specification, and a side-by-side oxide comparison against Chang'e-5 returned mare soil.

Growth-anchored transcriptomics. NASA OSD-476 grew Arabidopsis thaliana in 900 mg of Apollo 11, 12 and 17 regolith against a JSC-1A simulant control. Its ISA-Tab deposit keys each RNA-seq sample to a growth plate and a twelve-timepoint leaf-count trajectory, so each sequenced plant can be joined to its own growth (twelve one-to-one joins, four plate-mean joins; Spearman rho = 0.84 between two independently measured phenotype layers). Correlating expression against growth identifies 2,008 genes at 5% FDR for leaf-emergence rate, of which 299 replicate in an Apollo-only analysis where substrate no longer tracks growth, and 82 are not detected by the published substrate contrasts.

Contents. Acquisition and analysis code (scripts/, reproducible end to end via run_all.sh), derived tables and figures (results/), a static web database with in-browser ArUco scale and colour calibration (src/, public/), a LaTeX manuscript with a Crossref-verified bibliography and supplementary tables (manuscript/), and the ported precursor write-up (legacy/). Provenance, licence and SHA-256 for every input file are in MANIFEST.tsv; large re-fetchable NASA tables are listed there but not redistributed.

Licensing. Code MIT; data, figures and prose CC-BY-4.0. NASA OSDR and PSI data retain their own terms — cite the original investigators.
notes: Large NASA tables that the pipeline re-fetches on demand (chiefly the 36 MB GLDS-476 differential-expression table and the full-resolution OSD-670 imagery) are catalogued in MANIFEST.tsv with source URL and checksum but are not included in this archive. Run scripts/run_all.sh to reconstruct them.
